# T1-M3 final main-push maintenance source checkpoint

## Current state and causal scope

**Dormant source; actual M2 registration is `PENDING`.** This checkpoint does
not change the dEchorate workflow, enable a skip, create a new research result,
or complete M1/M2 qualification. Its independent source/contract must first be
protected; the later change that connects it remains confined to the existing
dEchorate workflow. The source-only event-range layer remains separate and
never grants a skip itself.

The contract follows [#759](https://github.com/jiying2007/audio-pipeline/issues/759),
including the finite 2026-10-20 06:39 UTC sequencing correction, and the three
independent direct-PR consumers in
[#758](https://github.com/jiying2007/audio-pipeline/issues/758). The old failed
dEchorate/PCR runs remain negative evidence. No red run or missing original
artifact is rewritten into a positive receipt.

The verified defect is temporal scope: the old diagnostic scope interpreted all
changes since the historical research ancestor as the current push. The earlier
source helper separates immutable science from current event scope. This final
helper adds only the later, explicit nonmeasurement disposition for the exact
merged Dependabot #714 proposal. It does not run a corpus, score audio, change a
threshold, approve an Action's implementation, or qualify HIL/product hardware.

## Source and event identity

The future maintenance job must check out the exact protected event base with
credentials disabled. For push this is `event.before`; candidate `after` and PR
head are read only as Git objects. Before importing a first-party dependency,
the helper checks its ordinary `100644` Git blob, full content identity and local
bytes against that base. The executed helper itself must match those bytes.
External Git configuration, shallow/grafted history and redirected object
contexts are rejected. No candidate Python, shell or workflow is executed by the
qualifier.

The original M1/T0/current witness and the run-bound M2 consumer have a fixed
four-file source closure. The final push helper and its registry also appear in
the source-range helper's exact fourth workflow profile. These source identities
do not certify that the original data was run or that a prerequisite stage closed.

| Identity | Required proof |
| --- | --- |
| Repository | Exact `jiying2007/audio-pipeline`, immutable repository ID `1347377137`, same repository in event, PR, run and artifact source |
| PR author | Merged, non-draft PR `714`, `dependabot[bot]`, actor ID `49699333`, type `Bot`, exact registered head ref |
| Push | Direct existing, non-forced main push; full nonzero `before`/`after`; `GITHUB_SHA` and `head_commit.id` equal `after` |
| Git transition | Actual `after` has exactly one parent `before`; complete PR head has `before` ancestry; PR head tree equals squash tree |
| Merge executor | The actual merged PR `merged_by`, push `sender`, run `actor`, `GITHUB_ACTOR` and `GITHUB_ACTOR_ID` agree; this identity is separate from the Bot PR author |
| Current run | Exact run ID/attempt, workflow file, repository, event, head SHA, branch, workflow ID, run number, actor and triggering actor; running status with no conclusion |
| Main protection | Current API and canonical public Git main ref both equal `after`; Ruleset `21804005` remains strict summary, squash-only, resolved threads and zero bypass |

All current main/rules/PR/run facts are read again after evidence processing.
An ordinary rerun may have a different triggering actor; its exact real metadata
must agree with the current environment and remain stable. The merged PR author
is never replaced with the person who requested that rerun.

`run.pull_requests[]` is not execution-SHA evidence. The public API actually
changed that association on old failed run
[38512536044](https://github.com/jiying2007/audio-pipeline/actions/runs/38512536044)
after the PR was rebased, while its own `head_sha` retained the old executed
commit. The new helper ignores that array; legitimate array changes do not
invalidate a fixed execution identity, and a wrong `head_sha` cannot be rescued
by a convenient association.

## Complete current-base Action transition

The helper invokes the same protected `classify_repo` and `expected_repo`
functions used by M1. Only their Git IO adapter is bound to the exact protected
checkout. It does not copy a weaker classifier or call the open-PR-only
`M1.live_probe` after the PR has merged.

The expected matrix is independently derived from every applicable Action use
site in `before`. Both actual `before -> PR head` and actual `before -> after`
must equal that complete matrix. The October 20 reviewed upload and CodeQL
transitions remain exact full SHA pairs. There is no 108/125/127-count exception:
new reviewed use sites on protected main participate automatically. Partial
updates, mixed C/config changes, workflow logic/permission edits, unknown pins,
renames and executable/symlink modes request the original scientific guards.

The source-range helper independently validates the original diagnostic,
manifests, predecessor identities, official corpus map and complete before
workflow template. Its fourth exact profile is registered as literal complete
source, with only the already reviewed all-use-site upload pin variant. It
retains the original scientific steps, permissions, timeout and diagnostic
condition. There is no arbitrary job, shell or YAML slot.

## Existing M2 prerequisites and fresh original receipts

The checked-in registry intentionally has no future run IDs. Its three
integration entries, qualifying protected main and matching Verify/Release
records are `null`, and its status is `PENDING`. Missing registration is a safe
negative before public network access.

When the already required M2 stage has actually closed, its real independent
workflow-only PR/merge identities and exact qualifying main Verify/Release
run/attempts can populate this record during the separately protected source
qualification. This records the existing stage; it adds no second approval
process. It does not claim to remeasure the previously reviewed corpus. The
helper reads those records back and verifies same-repository squash ancestry,
three distinct integrations, single-workflow change scope and main ancestry.
After validating each historical PR's exact registered identity, its original
head is fetched as data from the fixed canonical repository. A squash does not
make that head an ancestor of main, so a fresh main checkout cannot be assumed
to contain it. Missing upstream objects deny qualification; no local sibling
branch or alternate object cache supplies an implicit prerequisite. The second
metadata readback does not refetch or reinterpret the original identities.
The two PCR workflow blobs must still match their qualified protected main.
dEchorate's subsequent exact fourth profile is its explicit separately reviewed
workflow-only transition.

At the eventual merged-714 push, the latest direct PR runs are discovered anew
for the exact bot head and each of the three registered workflow files. Selection
uses the highest unique workflow run number from a complete bounded API list,
then checks both current run and exact attempt endpoints. It never guesses an
attempt from artifact timestamps or names. The current successful direct run
must have a successful maintenance job and explicitly skipped scientific jobs.
PCR02's nested Real AEC call is not a third direct workflow run.

The original direct-PR run's `actor` and `triggering_actor` each retain their
actual login and type together with the immutable actor ID. Each tuple must agree
across the current/attempt endpoints and the independent second readback. They
need not be the Bot PR author. A human
may trigger `synchronize` for the same already qualified Bot proposal or request
a rerun without changing its author, tree or scientific authority. The protected
M2 evaluator already admits that exact proposal independently of the triggerer;
the push consumer preserves that boundary while still requiring all three real
run-bound originals. Changing any execution actor during readback is a negative.

Each original artifact must pass all of the following checks:

1. Its precise `workflow-pin-maintenance-<workflow-stem>-<run_id>` name is unique
   in the selected run's complete bounded list. All three run IDs, artifact IDs
   and full ZIP digests must be distinct.
2. Its API source tuple (`workflow_run.id`, repository IDs, branch and executed
   head SHA) matches the actual selected direct run. The artifact is unexpired
   and has an exact API SHA256 digest and bounded size.
3. The entire original ZIP is read, and its size/SHA256 match that API record.
   A bounded public resolver supplies only the GitHub Azure storage redirect;
   the API digest and source tuple remain the authority. No authentication
   token or signed storage URL is printed or saved.
4. The archive contains one non-executable regular `maintenance.json`, at most
   16,000 bytes. Extra members, traversal, symlinks, malformed or encrypted
   archives and invalid/duplicate-key/nonfinite JSON fail closed. Nothing is
   extracted or executed.
5. The receipt's integer `run_id` and `run_attempt` equal the actual selected
   API run/attempt. A prior attempt's genuine receipt cannot become evidence
   of a rerun. Old receipts without those fields remain old negative evidence.
6. Its exact workflow/event/base/head/consumer and nonmeasurement decision agree.
   Its nested M1 fields must equal the freshly computed complete Git proof and
   protected source/witness identities. Its original synthetic PR event is
   fetched as data and must have exactly `[before, PR head]` parents and the PR
   tree.
7. The run, attempt, jobs and original artifact metadata are independently read
   again. Any change denies the maintenance decision.

The public API or original archive may be unavailable or expire. That produces
a negative with the original guards still required. It never allows substitution
of a newly fabricated JSON receipt, current green UI, stale run association or
one original reused under three names.

## Result, budgets and subsequent integration

Only complete, stable proof can emit
`SCIENCE_NOT_EXECUTED_NON_MEASUREMENT_MAIN_PUSH` with `skip_measurement=true`.
The result still states `scientific_experiment_executed=false`,
`acoustic_pass=false`, `corpus_materialized_or_verified=false` and
`action_supply_chain_attested=false`. Every negative keeps all skip/admission
fields false. Receipts and SHA256 seals are created exclusively; previous
evidence is never overwritten.

The future exact job retains its 5-minute timeout. The CLI's internal wall budget
is 240 seconds; individual Git calls remain 45 seconds, metadata and small
archive requests 15 seconds, metadata 150,000 bytes, each original ZIP 65,536
bytes, and the output receipt 16,000 bytes. No scientific timeout or retention
requirement is relaxed. The public metadata transport has no credentials; rate
limits and any unknown response remain explicit safe negatives.

The source/helper registry must become protected before the separate dEchorate
workflow-only integration. The human integration PR and its new main must really
run and verify the original fixed diagnostic, plus their existing full Verify
and matching Release requirements. Only after all three actual M2 integrations
close and the newest Bot proposal is requalified may the final workflow invoke
this main-push decision. No source checkpoint claims those future actions ran.

## Local verification

```sh
python3 .github/program/test_dechorate_push_maintenance_t1m3.py --self-test
python3 .github/program/test_dechorate_event_source_t1m3.py --self-test
python3 .github/program/workflow_pin_pr_consumer.py --self-test
```

The push tests create real commit, parent, tree, mode and complete Action
transitions from the real reachable repository history. The actual M2 evaluator
produces the local engineering receipts from that Git proof. Only HTTP/ref and
ZIP transport metadata are explicitly offline fixtures. Their `COMPLETE`
registration and positive metadata exist only in disposable engineering Git
objects; the checked-in record remains `PENDING`. The tests neither call the live
M1 probe nor download a scientific corpus and are not actual M1/M2, runner,
artifact, acoustic or product qualification.

中文边界：这是最终 push 维护判定的未接通源码检查点。来源层阳性、离线 Git
工程夹具、依赖维护跳过和原科学实验通过是不同事实。现有 M2 资格尚缺就保持
`PENDING`；必须先把真实既有阶段记录填入并保护源码，再用独立工作流改动接通。
不得把候选 Action 代码、历史关联 PR 数组、旧重跑原件或绿色状态代替当前原始证据。
